The left subfigure (a) illustrates training loss as a function of optimization progress for several methods (Vanilla, StrmLLM, and multiple SepLLM variants) plotted together on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “steps” and uses a linear scale; the numeric tick labels and exact range are present but not fully legible at the provided resolution. The y-axis is labeled as loss (training loss) on a linear scale, with visible gridlines and a range that appears to span roughly from the mid–1.x values up to the low–2.x values (exact tick labels are not fully legible). Multiple solid lines are shown with distinct colors and markers corresponding to the legend: a red line for Vanilla, and additional lines for StrmLLM and SepLLM configurations in other colors (including orange, green, purple, and blue tones) with small point markers at intervals. Across the x-axis, each line trends downward overall (loss decreasing with increasing steps), with the curves separating and then flattening to varying degrees toward the right side of the plot; precise numeric start/end values and any exact minima are not readable from the image.

The right subfigure (b) illustrates the ratio of loss values relative to the Vanilla baseline as a function of computation, with the same set of methods indicated by the legend. The x-axis is labeled “Total FLOPs” on a linear scale; the exact numeric range and tick values are present but not fully legible at the provided resolution. The y-axis is labeled “Loss Ratio w.r.t. Vanilla” on a linear scale, with a visible upper region near 1.0 and lower values extending below that (exact tick labels are not fully legible). The Vanilla series is drawn as a red line with markers that stays at a ratio of 1 across the plot, consistent with a self-normalized baseline, while the other method lines (shown in orange/green/purple/blue hues with distinct markers) begin near 1 toward the left and then move below 1 as FLOPs increase, with some curves dipping and then partially rising or flattening near the right side; exact ratio values at specific FLOPs and any precise minima are not readable from the image.
